description: The System Advisor Model (SAM) is a free techno-economic simulation program for renewable electricity generation projects, used by project managers, engineers, policy analysts, technology developers and researchers. It is developed by the National Laboratory of the Rockies, formerly the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, with contributors including Nate Blair, Paul Gilman, Janine Freeman, Nicholas DiOrio, Mark Mehos, Craig Turchi, Michael Wagner and Aron Dobos. Performance models cover photovoltaics from rooftop to utility scale, battery storage, concentrating solar power (trough, tower and linear Fresnel), industrial process heat, wind from single turbines to farms, wave and tidal energy, solar water heating, fuel cells, geothermal, biomass and high-concentration PV. Financial models cover behind-the-meter residential and commercial projects, power purchase agreement projects with single owners, partnership flips or leasebacks, and third-party ownership. The desktop program builds from open-source repositories, with the SSC compute modules usable directly through a software development kit. Coverage is not tied to a place. SAM is free to download, with source on GitHub under the BSD 3-Clause licence, and is actively maintained (53 tags, latest commit July 2026). Caveats: it simulates individual projects, not grids. Simulation uses are resource and project performance estimates that feed capacity planning. Related records: data-gridpath-india-planning-model-data uses PySAM outputs.
